orchestrator_output.text_narration: When an object changes its position with time, we say it is in motion. In our daily life, we see different things moving in different ways, such as a marching soldier, a spinning top, or a swinging pendulum. Based on how objects move, motion is divided into different types. Rectilinear motion is motion along a straight line. When an object moves in a straight path without changing direction, it is in rectilinear motion. For example, a car moving on a straight road or soldiers marching in a parade move along a straight line. Circular motion happens when an object moves along a circular path at a fixed distance from a central point, like a stone tied to a string being whirled around. Rotational motion happens when an object turns around its own central axis, like the blades of a ceiling fan or a spinning top. Periodic motion is a motion that repeats itself after a fixed equal interval of time. When a swing moves back and forth, or a pendulum moves from side to side, it repeats its motion regularly. This repeating movement at equal time intervals is called periodic motion.
